items.rationale: Locating both active supply leaks is covered under §§2.4.2 and 7.1.7(e). The €567 benchmark assumes the flat rate does not duplicate the separately billed labour or measurements.
Mapping moisture in the kitchen floor and wall is necessary under §7.1.7(e). The benchmark is €229 for one survey.
Six hours are consistent with the documented search for two leaks and are valued at €469 under §7.1.7(g), provided the labour is not already included in line 1 (§7.1.8(c)).
Section 7.1.7(g) allows necessary assisting labour at the helper rate. The six documented hours benchmark at €400, subject to the duplicate-cost rule in §7.1.8(c).
This is the first separately stated travel charge on the leak-detection invoice. Section 7.1.7(f) allows one such charge, benchmarked at €84.
The documented tracer gas and expendable isolation materials support a €47 allowance under §7.1.7(c) and (e). Reusable contractor equipment remains excluded under §7.1.8(b).
Opening the wall along the failed run is necessary access under §§7.1.1(b) and 7.1.7(a). Allow €245 for one opening operation, broader than the under-sink access in the reference cases.

items.description: Remove and dispose of soaked pipe lagging
items.rationale: Removal of the soaked foam lagging qualifies under §7.1.7(a). The 0.75-hour line benchmarks at €58 and is distinct from cavity-wool removal.

items.description: Remove and dispose of wet cavity wool
items.rationale: The saturated mineral wool was removed bay by bay and is covered under §7.1.7(a). The six-hour benchmark is €464; this is not a duplicate of the foam-lagging line.
The roof-space stain predates the plumbing loss and came from chimney flashing. Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) exclude this work; €380 is the conditional benchmark for a covered small-room drying job.
Section 7.1.7(b) and (e) covers hire of the single dryer used in the affected kitchen. The benchmark is €60 for the unit.
Both fans are billed for the unrelated roof space, so §§7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) exclude the line. The kitchen blower does not substantiate this charge; the conditional benchmark for two fans is €56.

Section 7.1.7(b) covers drying the measured kitchen moisture, not the full 50 m² tariff capacity. Allow €430 for the affected kitchen and cavity in the roughly 30 m² room, excluding separately billed hire and measurements.

The documented failed indoor supply connection qualifies under §2.4.3(a), with like-for-like repair under §7.1.1(b). Allow €155 for the one-metre repair, without duplicating fitting or technician charges.
The description confirms a reducer at each end of the replaced run. Section 7.1.7(c) allows two matching fittings at about €24 each, or €48 gross.
The three metres between the branches were split or sagging and required like-for-like replacement under §§2.4.3(a) and 7.1.7(c). Allow €42 per metre, or €126 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers equivalent lagging on the replaced run. Three metres at approximately €15 per metre give €45 gross.

Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour attributable to the documented repairs. The four-hour benchmark is €360, provided the time is not already billed in a repair or drying flat rate (§7.1.8(c)).

items.description: Installer labour to restore pipe lagging
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(c) and (g) cover reinstating lagging removed because of the loss or necessary access, not relagging merely because a pipe was exposed. Allow about three necessary hours at €85, or €255, rather than six hours for the broader scope.
The final readings confirmed completion of kitchen drying and are covered under §7.1.7(e). Allow €131 for the distinct final survey.

Vacuuming plaster dust and clearing board and vinyl scraps is repair-debris removal under §5.2.1, not general cleaning under §7.1.8(a). Allow the €206 site-cleaning benchmark without duplicating the insulation disposal lines.
Section 7.1.7(h) expressly covers removing the damaged furnishing from the dwelling when replaced. Allow €57 for the single removal.
Section 7.1.7(h) covers transport away from the dwelling. Allow €60 for the haul, separate from removal and disposal.
Actual disposal of the ruined insured table qualifies under §§5.2.1 and 7.4. Allow €38 for disposal alone, putting transport and disposal together at €98.
Section 7.1.1(d) pays current value, not new-for-old absent an endorsement. A comparable plain pine table at about €325 new, less roughly 45% for seven years of daily use and wear, gives about €180.
Delivery is separately covered by §7.1.7(h) and is not subject to depreciation on the table itself. Allow €60 for one delivery.
Necessary setup is covered under §7.1.7(h). Allow €90 for ordinary assembly of a plain pine table, consistent with the €150 reference for delivery and assembly less €60 for delivery.
Section 7.1.7(h) covers cleaning the table's footprint, not repeat cleaning of the kitchen repair area. Allow €41 for that specific task.
The patio furniture is kept outdoors and was not affected by the kitchen leak. Sections 4.2.6, 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(f) exclude the inspection; €75 is the conditional benchmark for a short inspection.
